subject: Re: TTFT & streaming SLOs — follow-up and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Cara Liu <cara@acme-retail.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 10 Jan 2027 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: TTFT & streaming SLOs — follow-up and next steps

Thanks again for the call this morning — great discussion and I wanted to capture the key items we agreed on and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth.

Recap (performance / SLO focus):
- Primary goal: Time-to-first-token (TTFT) target of <= 150 ms p50 for 1-2 token responses at peak traffic for the checkout assistant.
- Streaming: real-time streaming required for multi-turn assistant flows. Preferred transport: SSE for web clients; WebSocket allowed for mobile app.
- Chunk cadence: target <= 100 ms between chunks during streaming (aim for 50–100 ms to keep UI responsive).
- Throughput / concurrency: steady-state 200 RPS (inference requests) with bursts up to 1,000 RPS during promotional events; target concurrency for tail calls ~400 concurrent sessions.
- Fallback behavior: graceful degrade to a lower-cost model variant if latency breach > 500 ms or capacity constraints.

Open questions from our side (we noted on the call):
1) Can you share a small representative request/response payload (1–3 examples) and typical token counts for user prompts and assistant responses?
2) Do you have an existing SSE/WebSocket client implementation we can test against, or should we provide a reference client?
3) Any strict RTT limits from your CDN or edge infra that we should be aware of (e.g., <50 ms RTT requirements)?

Proposed next steps:
- I attached a short perf template (acme_perf_requirements.xlsx) — please fill the example rows and return by EOD Tue so Vivek and I can size a focused perf run.
- Vivek will propose a perf test config (load profile + model variant + batching) and a proposed test date (we recommended Wed or Thu next week).
- Schedule a 45-min POC kickoff where we walk through the load shape and run an initial baseline. I sent a calendar invite (redwood_demo-invite.ics) — feel free to propose a different time.

If that all looks right I'll book the perf window and loop in our SRE to coordinate network details.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0113

Attachments: acme_perf_requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Cara Liu <cara@acme-retail.com>

Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@acme-retail.com>, Acme SRE Team <sre@acme-retail.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 08:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: TTFT & streaming SLOs — follow-up and next steps

Thanks Marissa — this is perfect and captures the call. Quick answers inline: 

> Primary goal: TTFT <= 150 ms p50
Yes, 150 ms p50 is our target. We also want p95 < 300 ms if feasible.

> Chunk cadence target <= 100 ms
We’d prefer ~60–80 ms chunk cadence for the best UX on mobile.

> Throughput / concurrency
Confirmed: 200 RPS steady, planning for 1,000 RPS burst traffic. Our infra team expects ~350 concurrent open sessions during peak cart-checkflow.

Answers to your open questions:
1) Payload examples: Attached two sanitized examples (user_prompt_example.txt, assistant_expected.txt) in a follow-up email (I’ll send after this). Typical prompt tokens ~25–40, expected assistant tokens ~8–20.
2) We have a lightweight SSE reference client maintained by our web team — I’ll share the repo link with SRE after the perf template is filled.
3) RTT: our primary CDN edge is usually 25–40 ms RTT in the US regions we care about. Not <50 ms hard limit, but lower is better.

We’ll fill the perf template and return it by Tue end-of-day. Please proceed to propose test window options.

—Cara
Sr. Product Manager, AI Experience | Acme Retail
cara@acme-retail.com

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: TTFT & streaming SLOs — follow-up and next steps

Thanks — a few technical clarifications from infra side to make the perf run productive: 

- Transport: SSE is fine for web and simpler to implement for an initial test. WebSocket gives bidirectional control if you plan to send client-side typing indicators; both are supported by our runtime.
- Chunk cadence vs batch sizing: To hit ~60–100 ms chunk cadence we’ll need to tune micro-batching windowing. For the payload sizes you described (25–40 tokens in, 8–20 tokens out) we expect to achieve ~100 ms TTFT on a 16GB-quantized model instance with continuous batching disabled for the first token (we prioritize TTFT over batching for small requests).
- Test config I’ll propose: 1) baseline single-client p50/p95; 2) synthetic steady-state 200 RPS for 15 minutes; 3) 5 x 1-minute bursts ramping to 1,000 RPS. We’ll measure TTFT, chunk cadence distribution, CPU/GPU utilization, and observed queueing latency.
- Network: please confirm a public test endpoint or provide a temporary VPN/whitelisted IPs for our test harness. If you prefer, we can run from our Hosted region in us-west with edge-to-edge measurements.

I’ll draft a perf job and post the config to the shared drive link Marissa included. If p95 > 300 ms during steady-state we’ll look at enabling a higher-throughput model variant + larger batch slots as a mitigation.

—Vivek
Infra Lead, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
vivek@redwood.ai
